comment: Declarative asset manifest for d2rim. `tools/assets/fetch-assets.mjs` is the only
thing that reads it; nothing else in the project may hardcode an asset URL.
NETWORK REALITY (re-measured 2026-07-26; the earlier note here was partly wrong).
REACHABLE: registry.npmjs.org, raw.githubusercontent.com, and -- contrary to the previous
note -- cdn.jsdelivr.net, data.jsdelivr.com, unpkg.com and gitlab.com raw. BLOCKED (403 at
CONNECT): Poly Haven, ambientCG, Kenney.nl, Quaternius, Mixamo, Freesound, OpenGameArt,
Sketchfab, poly.pizza, the CMU mocap library, threejs.org, github.com, api.github.com and
codeload.github.com.
The jsDelivr correction is what unlocked the KayKit packs. codeload is still blocked, so we
cannot download a repo tarball and we get no listing from the GitHub API -- but
data.jsdelivr.com/v1/packages/gh/<owner>/<repo>@<ref>?structure=flat returns a FULL FILE TREE
for any public GitHub repo. That is the directory listing this pipeline previously lacked.
Discovery therefore goes through data.jsdelivr.com; the actual bytes are still fetched from
raw.githubusercontent.com, so every `path` below remains an exact, verified path.
npm is the other listing channel: an npm tarball is its own directory listing, which is how
aframe-enviropacks (90 MB of vendored Poly Haven + ambientCG art) was found.
LICENSING RULE. An asset is only in the `core` tier if its licence is documented at
source in a file we can fetch and archive. `licenseEvidence` names that file, and the
fetcher downloads it alongside the asset so the claim is auditable offline. Anything
whose licence we cannot prove lives in the `review-required` tier and is NOT downloaded
unless the operator passes --include-review-required.

CC0-1.0.name: Creative Commons Zero v1.0 Universal (public domain dedication)

LicenseRef-Mixamo-Unclear.name: Mixamo-derived, redistribution rights unresolved
LicenseRef-Mixamo-Unclear.notes: Adobe's terms permit use of Mixamo content inside a project but restrict standalone redistribution. The hosting repositories publish no per-asset grant that we can verify (three.js's MIT LICENSE covers the library, not the example art; BabylonJS blanket-relabels its mixamo/ subtree CC BY 4.0, which is a claim it is not obviously entitled to make). Prototype-only pending a human legal decision.

pmndrs-assets.comment: Self-hosted on npm, so it is immune to the CDN egress block. This is our stand-in for Poly Haven: the HDRIs ship as base64 data-URI JS modules that the `data-uri-module` transform decodes back into real .exr binaries.

three-examples.comment: Pinned to tag r185 (matching our three dependency) rather than the moving `dev` branch, so a re-fetch a year from now returns identical bytes. NOTE: three.js publishes per-asset licences for only a handful of examples. We take exactly one asset from here -- the one with an explicit CC0 README.

khronos-samples.comment: Licences are per-model and stated in each Models/<name>/README.md. There is no repo-wide grant, so every asset taken from here names its README as licenceEvidence.

kaykit-adventurers.comment: Kay Lousberg's Adventurers pack, mirrored by the author to GitHub (org KayKit-Game-Assets), which is how it reaches us at all -- kaylousberg.itch.io is 403 at CONNECT. Repo-root LICENSE.txt states CC0 1.0 in full prose, so this is licence evidence in the strong sense: an asset-specific grant written by the author, not an npm `license` field describing code. Untagged, so pinned to `main` like khronos-samples; the lock's sha256 is what actually detects drift.

kaykit-skeletons.comment: Same author, same licence file, same 41-joint rig as the Adventurers pack -- which is the whole reason it is here. Skeletons are literal Act I enemies (Den of Evil, Burial Grounds, Cathedral) and sharing a skeleton with the Barbarian means one retarget path covers player and enemy alike.

kaykit-dungeon.comment: Modular dungeon kit, 204 self-contained .glb props (buffers AND textures embedded -- verified, no sidecar .bin/.png to chase). Supplies the encampment/cave set dressing: barrels, crates, torches, rubble, walls, floors, stairs.

aframe-enviropacks.comment: The single most valuable thing on npm for this project: a 90 MB tarball that vendors real Poly Haven (then 'HDRI Haven'/'Texture Haven') and ambientCG (then 'CC0 Textures') PBR sets at 2K, plus Poly Haven HDRIs. Those two sites are 403 for us, so this package is the ONLY route to genuine photoscanned PBR art in this container. Its Readme.md attributes each asset class to its upstream and states CC0 for HDRIs and textures explicitly -- that sentence is the licence evidence we archive. NOTE: the same Readme does NOT make a clean CC0 claim for its bundled .glb models, so we take zero models from here.

kenney-rpg-audio.comment: Kenney's RPG Audio pack. kenney.nl is 403 for us, so the bytes come from a third-party GitHub mirror of the Kenney donation bundle -- but we deliberately do NOT rely on that mirror's own licence claim. The `licenseEvidence` for every file here points at Kenney's OWN pack-specific License.txt, which we fetch from the `excalibur` npm package (see the `excalibur` source). Bytes from the mirror, grant from the author.

excalibur.comment: Present ONLY as a licence-evidence carrier. The Excalibur game engine vendors one file of Kenney's RPG Audio pack together with Kenney's verbatim License.txt ('RPG Audio by Kenney Vleugels (Kenney.nl) / License (Creative Commons Zero, CC0)'). That file is a first-party, pack-specific CC0 grant for exactly the audio we take from the mirror above, which is a far stronger claim than a mirror repo's blanket LICENSE.md. No Excalibur bytes ship in the game.

uisfx.comment: 936 synthesised interface sounds in 12 timbre families, each as both .mp3 and .ogg. Notable for getting the licensing right: the package ships a SEPARATE `LICENSE-AUDIO` file dedicating the `sounds/` tree to CC0-1.0, distinct from the MIT `LICENSE` covering its code. That is exactly the art-specific statement this pipeline requires. We take the `organic` family, which is the least synthetic-sounding of the twelve.

kaykit-hexagon.comment: Same author and same CC0 LICENSE.txt as the other KayKit packs. Unlike them it ships .gltf + .bin + a SHARED hexagons_medieval.png atlas rather than self-contained .glb, so each model is three manifest entries' worth of files that must land in one directory: the .gltf references `<name>.bin` and `hexagons_medieval.png` as plain sibling URIs. Everything from this source therefore lands in models/hexkit/ together, and the atlas is fetched exactly once and shared by all of them. We take only the tent/fence/nature/prop pieces -- the hex tiles themselves are useless to a continuous-world game.

assets.usage: Blood Moor / overcast exteriors.
assets.selectionRationale: Chosen on measured radiance, not on filename. Decoded and analysed: mean luminance 0.699, blue/red ratio 1.80 (cool), peak/mean 57. That low peak/mean is the important number -- it means there is no hard sun disc, i.e. genuinely diffuse overcast light, which is exactly the cold flat key Act I wants. `park` and `sky` were rejected for peak/mean of 3958 and 29613 (harsh direct sun).

assets.usage: Rogue Encampment at dusk; the hub's default mood.
assets.selectionRationale: Mean luminance 0.409 (dim), blue/red 1.37 (cool-leaning rather than a warm tropical sunset), peak/mean 600 (a low sun disc is present and will read as a real light source). Cold dusk, not golden hour.

assets.usage: Den of Evil and all cave interiors.
assets.selectionRationale: Mean luminance 0.066 -- roughly 10x darker than the overcast plate -- and upper-hemisphere luminance 0.009, i.e. effectively black overhead. That near-zero ambient is the point: it lets torches and spell light dominate the interior instead of competing with an IBL floor.

assets.usage: High-frequency detail normal layered over procedural rock and cliff materials.
assets.selectionRationale: 512x512 and tiling. Verified as a real WebP (VP8 chunk, 512x512) by decoding the data URI.

assets.usage: Fine grain over mud, wet stone and worn wood.
assets.selectionRationale: 512x512 and tiling; finer grain than 0015, so the two layer without moire.

assets.usage: Bark and organic surfaces.
assets.selectionRationale: 512x512 and tiling; irregular organic pattern rather than a machined one.

assets.usage: THE PLAYER. Act I protagonist body and the animation source of truth for the locomotion and combat state machines.
assets.selectionRationale: This is the asset that closes the project's single biggest gap. Verified by parsing the GLB: 41 joints, 1 skin, 76 animation clips, one 1024 gradient atlas material (so it batches trivially). The clip set is not a stub -- it contains Idle, Walking_A/B/C, Walking_Backwards, Running_A/B, Running_Strafe_Left/Right, Hit_A/B, Death_A/B (+ settled death poses), Block/Blocking/Block_Hit, four 1H melee attacks, five 2H melee attacks, three dualwield attacks, dodges in four directions, PickUp, Interact and Use_Item. Every clip the brief asked for (idle/walk/run/attack/hit/death) ships authored; nothing needs to be faked. Licence is unambiguous CC0 prose from the author, so unlike Xbot and Big Vegas this one can actually ship.

credit.title: Forest ground 03 (albedo)
credit.author: Poly Haven (formerly Texture Haven / HDRI Haven)

assets.usage: The Blood Moor and every wet-earth exterior; the default ground material.
assets.selectionRationale: Photoscanned wet forest floor: dark, broken, organic, with leaf litter rather than clean soil. That is the Blood Moor read almost exactly, and it beats any procedural noise-based mud because the albedo carries real large-scale blotching that noise cannot fake at grazing angles.

credit.author: Poly Haven (formerly Texture Haven / HDRI Haven)

assets.usage: Dead/patchy grass over rock — the transition band between the moor and the cliffs.
assets.selectionRationale: Aerial (top-down) capture, so it tiles as terrain without the perspective smearing that eye-level grass scans have. Grass is already sparse and rock-broken, which desaturates toward "dead" convincingly with a colour grade instead of needing a different scan.

credit.title: Winter Lake 01
credit.author: Poly Haven (formerly Texture Haven / HDRI Haven)

assets.usage: The cold grey-sky key for the Blood Moor and Cold Plains — the overcast mood Act I actually wants.
assets.selectionRationale: The brief explicitly asked for an overcast/grey sky and the existing env.overcast (pmndrs "forest") is a green-tinted woodland plate, not a grey one. This is a genuine flat winter overcast: no sun disc, fully diffuse, desaturated. Taken at 2K because that is the only resolution shipped for this plate; it is the single largest asset added and is worth the 5.7 MB as the default exterior key.

credit.title: Large Corridor
credit.author: Poly Haven (formerly Texture Haven / HDRI Haven)

assets.usage: Enclosed stone interiors: the Cathedral, the Catacombs, the Jail levels.
assets.selectionRationale: A real interior capture, so the IBL carries bounce off nearby walls rather than sky. That is what makes an interior read as enclosed; the existing env.cave (pmndrs "night") is an exterior night sky and gives the wrong occlusion cues indoors.

credit.title: Moonless Golf

assets.usage: The darkest exterior key — deep cave mouths and night surface areas where torches must dominate.
assets.selectionRationale: Near-zero ambient with no moon disc, so practical lights (torches, spells) carry the entire frame. Complements env.cave, which still has a faint sky term.

assets.usage: Player and NPC footfalls; pick round-robin per step event.
assets.selectionRationale: Kenney ships ten takes of the same footfall specifically so a walk cycle can randomise without an audible loop. We take eight, which is past the point where repetition is perceptible. These are soft/earthy takes, so they suit mud and dirt directly; stone can be approximated by driving them through a brighter EQ and a short reverb send rather than needing a second sample set.

credit.title: KayKit Medieval Hexagon Pack — hexagons_medieval atlas
credit.author: Kay Lousberg

assets.usage: The single shared gradient atlas for EVERY model in models/hexkit/.
assets.selectionRationale: One 15 KB atlas textures all twelve hexkit models, because the pack uses a gradient-palette workflow rather than per-model UV maps. That is why the whole kit costs one texture and one material, and why every .gltf above must sit in the same directory as this file.
